{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish at the very start and drew it on the pad. The outline reads clearly with a big rounded body and a forked tail. I laid the start domino and the first stroke, the top of the body from the nose, which everything else grows from. As a result about 130 of the 145 standing dominoes were connected to the start when the push came, and the body and both tails were lit.

Execution
I sketched the fish with curves rather than corners so one push could run through it, and I numbered the strokes so each person had a clear piece. I closed the gap near the nose so the top curve connected. When the lower tail wouldn't catch at the crossing, I relaid it from scratch and it lit up. I also inspected the crossing, tails and loop several times to see what would actually fall. I worked on the tail loop on the right until late, and it did not light up in the end.

Collaboration
I gave Sofia, Omar and Jack each a stroke and told them to start once the lines reached them. I asked people to keep clear of the spots I was working on, so we didn't bump each other. I took Sofia's offer to fix the notch from the top while I worked from below. In the last two minutes I asked everyone to go hands-off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Leadership
I set the plan in the first seconds: the animal, the sketch and who did which stroke. I kept the table coordinated and kept updating everyone on what I was doing. I made the call to stop working on the loop and protect the lit body and tails, and kept everyone's hands off for the final stretch.", "my_share_percent": 40}
